solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Weight you lost back in the day (4)

indicatorNotes.lost: the weight has lost the letter standing for 'you', so it drops out

blocks.note: an ounce is a unit of weight
U, text-speak for 'you', is taken out of OUNCE

annotation.surface: A dieter looking back wistfully on the pounds they shed years ago.
annotation.walkthrough: U standing for 'you' is text-message shorthand. 'Back in the day' reads like part of the dieting story but is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Once means at some time in the past, which is what 'back in the day' says.

entries.clue: You might say an artist in residence (10)

blocks.note: asked what you do for a living, you might say 'an artist': a definition by example
residence as the act of living in a house, as a tenant does

annotation.surface: An artist in residence, a painter given a studio by a college or gallery.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Artist in residence' reads as one fixed phrase; split it after 'artist' and the 'in' is only a joint between two definitions.
annotation.definitionFit: Artist is an answer to 'What is your occupation?', and occupation also means living in a place.

entries.clue: Disturbance curtailed by copper is a rare thing (5)

indicatorNotes.curtailed: to curtail is to cut the tail off, so the last letter goes
indicatorNotes.by: beside: the copper goes next to the shortened word

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
RIOT without its last letter

annotation.surface: A rare disturbance being cut short by a police officer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Copper' pretends to be a police officer arriving at the riot; here it is the metal.
annotation.definitionFit: A curio is an unusual object prized for its rarity.

entries.clue: Ongoing issue for one wrecked on Madeira? (10)

annotation.definition: Ongoing issue for one wrecked on Madeira?

blocks.note: a lasting problem someone lives with
the surface wants a shipwreck on the Atlantic island; wrecked is slang for very drunk, and Madeira is the fortified wine

annotation.surface: A castaway shipwrecked on the island of Madeira, with a long-running problem.
annotation.walkthrough: Madeira is an Atlantic island and also the wine made there; wrecked is slang for very drunk, so the castaway turns into a drinker.
annotation.definitionFit: Alcoholism is the lasting problem of someone repeatedly drunk on wine.

entries.clue: Roast meat served with endless lasagne? (7)

indicatorNotes.served with: put on the plate alongside, so one piece follows the other
indicatorNotes.endless: without its ends: both the first and last letter go

blocks.note: lamb is a meat
lasagne is an example of PASTA; drop both ends to leave AST

annotation.surface: A roast joint put on the table beside a dish of lasagne.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that lasagne stands for its category, PASTA, not its own letters. 'Roast' looks like cooking but is the verb to criticise.
annotation.definitionFit: To lambast someone is to criticise them harshly, as a critic roasts them.

entries.clue: Out-of-head louts smoke in secret (7)

indicatorNotes.Out-of-head: the head, or first letter, is put out

blocks.note: louts are YOBS; without the head Y, OBS
to cure fish or meat can mean to smoke it

annotation.surface: Stoned hooligans lighting up where nobody can see them.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Out-of-head' reads as intoxicated, which suits the smoking louts; YOBS is British slang for louts.
annotation.definitionFit: Obscure means little known or hidden, so secret.

entries.clue: Senior is more daring going topless (5)

indicatorNotes.going topless: losing the top, the first letter in a down answer

blocks.note: bolder means more daring
the B at the top goes

annotation.surface: A pensioner growing more daring by sunbathing topless.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is saucy, but 'topless' just means the top letter comes off.
annotation.definitionFit: Senior means greater in age, which is older.

entries.clue: Your setter’s on strike with his boss? Shut up! (9)

indicatorNotes.on: in a down answer, one piece goes on top of the next

blocks.note: the setter is 'I', so 'your setter is' is I'M
to pound is to strike
the setter's boss is the editor, ED

annotation.surface: A crossword setter walking out with the editor, then being told to be quiet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On strike' sounds like industrial action; here 'on' only stacks I'M above POUND. The exclamation 'Shut up!' is really the past participle of shut up, meaning locked away.
annotation.definitionFit: Impounded means shut up in a pound, as a stray animal or towed car is.
annotation.definitionNote: reads as a command but means locked away, a past participle like the answer

entries.clue: Red targets released from trap (4)

indicatorNotes.released from trap: a trap is slang for the mouth, so words released from it are spoken

blocks.note: targets are MARKS, which is what gets spoken; the spelling that sounds the same names a famous Red

annotation.surface: A red target springing out of a trap, as at a clay-pigeon shoot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Trap' is slang for the mouth ('shut your trap'), so what leaves it is heard. Red is the usual label for a communist, and Karl Marx is the founding one.
annotation.definitionFit: Karl Marx, the father of communism, is the archetypal Red.

entries.clue: A vault cracked by one with ambitious plans? (8)

indicatorNotes.cracked by: the vault is broken open by the one, which goes inside

blocks.note: as written
to vault is to spring or leap
I is the Roman one; it goes inside SPRING to make SPIRING

annotation.surface: A safecracker with ambitious plans breaking into a bank vault.
annotation.walkthrough: The bank vault is a leap, SPRING. 'One with ambitious plans' tempts as the definition, but 'one' is only the I.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to aspire is to set your sights high, so a person who is aspiring has big plans.

entries.clue: My Charlie’s smartish pants (9)

indicatorNotes.pants: British slang for rubbish or badly done, so the letters are a mess

blocks.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
SMARTISH rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone showing off their boyfriend's rather smart trousers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'My' is the exclamation of surprise, and 'Christmas!' is another. In Britain pants are underpants and, as slang, rubbish.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Christmas!' is an old exclamation of surprise, just like 'My!'.

entries.clue: One administers drug in awkward operation (5)

indicatorNotes.in: the answer is found inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of awkwaRD into OPERation

annotation.surface: A medic giving a drug during a clumsy operation.
annotation.walkthrough: The hidden word straddles the gap between the two words, so read through the space.
annotation.definitionFit: A doper is one who administers drugs, especially to racehorses or athletes.

entries.clue: Bread having little bit of iron (5)

indicatorNotes.bit of: only a small piece, the first letter, is taken

blocks.note: poor means meagre or little
first letter of iron

annotation.surface: A loaf with a trace of iron in it, as a health label might boast.
annotation.walkthrough: Poori is a puffed, deep-fried Indian flatbread. 'Iron' tempts as FE, its chemical symbol, but only its first letter is wanted.
annotation.definitionFit: A poori is an Indian bread, deep-fried until it puffs up.

entries.clue: Tank with rear turned to small house (8)

indicatorNotes.with rear turned to: the last letter is changed into another

blocks.note: an aquarium is a fish tank
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small; it replaces the final M

annotation.surface: Converting a water tank at the back of a property into a little cottage.
annotation.walkthrough: 'House' here is astrological: the zodiac is divided into twelve houses, and Aquarius is one of them.
annotation.definitionFit: Aquarius is one of the twelve signs, or houses, of the zodiac.

entries.clue: Uncle is man without money heading for ruin (10)

indicatorNotes.heading for: the head, or first letter, of the next word

blocks.note: a chess piece is a man, and the pawn is the humblest
broke means having no money
first letter of ruin

annotation.surface: A penniless relative on the road to financial ruin.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Uncle' is old slang for a pawnbroker, so the relative is really the lender the penniless man visits.
annotation.definitionFit: Uncle is old slang for a pawnbroker, the lender who holds your goods against a loan.

entries.clue: Is tutor mistaken for lady who does? (7)

indicatorNotes.mistaken: the letters have been taken the wrong way, so rearrange them

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

annotation.surface: A private tutor being taken for the cleaning lady.
annotation.walkthrough: A 'lady who does' is British for a cleaner, but the question mark allows the other sense of 'do': a tourist does Rome or the Louvre.
annotation.definitionFit: A tourist is someone who does the sights, the sense of 'do' as in 'doing Paris'.

entries.clue: Around noon, a Parisian loved to get naked (9)

indicatorNotes.Around: the word for loved goes around the N

blocks.note: un is French for 'a'
adored means loved
N is the abbreviation for noon

annotation.surface: A Parisian at midday who loved stripping off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A Parisian' looks like a person, but it means the word 'a' as a Parisian would say it.
annotation.definitionFit: Unadorned means bare, without decoration, so naked.

entries.clue: English pal burying dead animal (7)

indicatorNotes.burying: the pal holds the dead inside it, like a grave

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
rhyming slang: china plate = mate
D is the abbreviation for dead, as in genealogies

annotation.surface: An English friend giving a dead pet a burial.
annotation.walkthrough: China is Cockney rhyming slang for a mate (china plate). The echidna is a spiny Australian anteater.
annotation.definitionFit: The echidna is a spiny egg-laying mammal of Australia and New Guinea.

entries.clue: Man with a rubbish complaint (4,4)

indicatorNotes.with: the pieces go together, one after another

blocks.note: he is a man
as written
trash is rubbish

annotation.surface: A man grumbling about the rubbish.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' reads as a grumble about bin collections but is a medical complaint, an ailment.
annotation.definitionFit: Heat rash is a skin ailment, and a complaint is any minor illness.

entries.clue: Abrupt official in outsize shades (7)

indicatorNotes.Abrupt: cut short, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
a park ranger is an official; cut short, RANGE

annotation.surface: A brusque official wearing oversized sunglasses.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shades' looks like sunglasses to go with the official, but it means colours.
annotation.definitionFit: Oranges are shades, meaning colours, like tangerine or amber.

entries.clue: I’m one to defend large, decisive blow (7)

indicatorNotes.to defend: to guard something by surrounding it

blocks.note: the one writing the clue is the setter
L is the clothing abbreviation for large

annotation.surface: A boxer defending with a big, fight-ending punch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'I'm one' is the setter speaking of himself. Settler here is the old sense: something that settles an argument or a fight.
annotation.definitionFit: A settler is a blow or argument that decides the matter, settling it.

entries.clue: Good man getting hot sandwiches with sub (5,2)

indicatorNotes.sandwiches: the first pieces hold the next between them, like bread round a filling

blocks.note: a saint is a good man, abbreviated ST
in means fashionable, hot
and means together with

annotation.surface: A good man eating hot sandwiches, the kind served in a sub roll.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sandwiches' and 'sub' both look like food; one is the container and the other the definition, a substitute.
annotation.definitionFit: A stand-in is a substitute, which is what sub is short for.

entries.clue: Uranium found in aslant, mutated fruit (7)

indicatorNotes.mutated: changed in form, so the letters rearrange

blocks.note: chemical symbol
anagram fodder, with U among it

annotation.surface: Radioactive uranium leaking at an angle and producing mutant fruit.
annotation.walkthrough: The radioactive surface makes 'mutated' look natural; it only tells you to rearrange ASLANT with the U inside.
annotation.definitionFit: A sultana is a dried white grape, a fruit.

entries.clue: Apish lot monkeying in theatre seat? (8)

indicatorNotes.monkeying: messing about, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: A troop of apes misbehaving in the stalls of a theatre.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Theatre' is the operating theatre, and a seat is where something is housed, so a hospital is the home of theatres.
annotation.definitionFit: A hospital is where operating theatres are sited, their seat.

entries.clue: Make a vinyl record for Squeeze (5)

blocks.note: vinyl discs are stamped out of hot plastic by a master disc
the plain verb, to push hard on something

annotation.surface: Cutting a vinyl album for Squeeze, the London pop band.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital S dresses 'Squeeze' up as the British band; capitals can be ignored, and it is the plain verb.
annotation.definitionFit: Records are pressed from a master, and to press is to squeeze.

entries.clue: Belligerent boatman? (5)

annotation.definitionNote: belligerent is used as a noun, a fighter

blocks.note: one who rows, rhyming with cows, is a quarreller
one who rows, rhyming with goes, a boat

annotation.surface: An aggressive man in a boat.
annotation.walkthrough: The same spelling has two pronunciations: a row (rhyming with cow) is a quarrel, and to row (rhyming with go) is to pull oars.
annotation.definitionFit: A rower is one who rows: either a quarrelsome person or an oarsman.

entries.clue: Spirit I polished off in anger (5)

indicatorNotes.polished off: to polish something off is to finish it or dispose of it, so the I is done away with

blocks.note: a wraith is a ghost, a spirit
the I is removed

annotation.surface: Someone angrily knocking back a glass of spirits.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' and 'polished off' suggest a drink downed in a temper; the spirit is a ghost.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, though wrath is the grander, biblical word for fierce anger.

entries.clue: Rocks primarily found in, say, cold gin? (4)

indicatorNotes.found in: the R is to be found inside the other word, so it goes within it

blocks.note: a cold tap is one example of a tap, hence 'say'
first letter of Rocks; it goes inside TAP

annotation.surface: Ordering gin on the rocks, with ice.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On the rocks' and 'gin' set up a bar order, but a gin is also a snare for animals. 'Say' shows that cold is an example of a tap.
annotation.definitionFit: A gin, as in gin trap, is a snare for catching animals.

entries.clue: Wander in grassland (5)

blocks.note: a verb: to roam freely over an area
a noun: the open grazing country of the American West

annotation.surface: Walking through open grassland.
annotation.walkthrough: Both halves live in the same prairie scene, which hides the join at 'in'.
annotation.definitionFit: To range is to roam, and the range is open grazing country.

entries.clue: One has undue interest in Noah’s ark out on lake (4,5)

indicatorNotes.out: not in order, so the letters rearrange
indicatorNotes.on: placed after: the jumbled letters sit on the L

blocks.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake
NOAHSARK rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone oddly fascinated by Noah's Ark afloat on a lake.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Undue interest' looks like obsession but is excessive interest on a loan.
annotation.definitionFit: A loan shark charges extortionate interest, which is undue interest.

entries.clue: Dull type passing on plates of meat? (10)

annotation.definition2: type passing on plates of meat?

blocks.note: an adjective: plodding, lacking any spark

blocks.clueFragment: type passing on plates of meat?
blocks.note: plates of meat is rhyming slang for feet

annotation.surface: A boring person turning down a dinner of meat.
annotation.walkthrough: Plates of meat is Cockney rhyming slang for feet, so the one going past on them is walking. 'Dull type' looks like one definition, but it splits after 'Dull'.
annotation.definitionFit: Pedestrian means dull, and a pedestrian is someone travelling on foot.

entries.clue: One who cleans burn (4)

blocks.note: a noun: a cleaning woman, in dated British usage
a verb: to scorch until blackened

annotation.surface: A cleaner with a burn.
annotation.walkthrough: A char is British for a cleaning woman, short for charwoman.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a British regional word for a cleaner, and a plain synonym for scorching wood or food black.
